packages.hook: I spent $240 on five AI tools that all promise to make you money. Three were a total waste. Two actually paid for themselves — and one free tool beat a $40-a-month paid one. Here's the exact breakdown, with receipts.
packages.hook_zh: 我花了 240 刀买了 5 个都说能帮你搞钱的 AI 工具。3 个纯纯智商税，2 个真回本了——其中还有一个免费工具，吊打了 40 刀/月的付费版。下面是带账单的完整拆解。

hook_options.label: 戳中『每月被 AI 订阅吸血』
hook_options.en: If you're paying twenty, forty, sixty dollars a month for AI tools that promise to make you rich, and you're still living paycheck to paycheck, you're not using AI to make money — you're paying a subscription fee to feel like you are. I stopped guessing and tested five of them for real.
hook_options.zh: 如果你每个月都在给那些『能让你搞钱』的 AI 工具交 20、40、60 刀的订阅费，结果你还是靠工资过日子——你不是在用 AI 搞钱，你是在交一笔『感觉自己在搞钱』的订阅税。我不再瞎猜，直接实测了 5 个。

hook_options.label: 打破『付费=更好』
hook_options.en: Everyone sells you the $40-a-month AI tool that'll make you rich. I bought five of the most hyped ones, ran them for thirty days, and the free tool beat two of the paid ones. The expensive one was the worst. Here's what actually happened.
hook_options.zh: 所有人都向你推销那个 40 刀/月、能让你暴富的 AI 工具。我买了 5 个最火的，实跑 30 天，结果免费工具吊打了其中两个付费的。最贵的那个反而最坑。下面是真实发生的事。

hook_options.label: 240 刀换一份避坑账本
hook_options.en: I burned $240 and thirty days testing five paid AI money-making tools so you don't have to. The result: three cancellations, two keepers, and one free tool that outperformed a paid one. Here's the full ledger, down to the cent.
hook_options.zh: 我花了 240 刀和 30 天，实测 5 个付费 AI 搞钱工具，就为了让你不用踩坑。结果：3 个退订、2 个留下、1 个免费工具比付费的还猛。下面是精确到分的完整账本。

titles: I Tested 5 Paid AI Tools to Make Money — Only 2 Actually Paid For Themselves
Stop Paying for AI Tools That Don't Make You Money (I Learned the Hard Way)

script.en: I spent $240 on five AI tools that all promise to make you money. Three were a total waste. Two actually paid for themselves — and one free tool beat a $40-a-month paid one. Here's the exact breakdown, with receipts.
script.zh: 我花了 240 刀买了 5 个都说能帮你搞钱的 AI 工具。3 个纯纯智商税，2 个真回本了——其中还有一个免费工具，吊打了 40 刀/月的付费版。下面是带账单的完整拆解。

script.en: By the end of this video you'll see the exact five tools I tested, what each one claims to do, which three I already cancelled, which two I'm keeping, and the free tool that quietly outperformed a paid one. Real accounts, real cancellations, zero affiliate links — I'm not getting paid to say any of this.
script.zh: 看完这条视频，你会看到我实测的这 5 个工具到底是什么、各自号称能干什么、我已经退掉哪 3 个、留下哪 2 个，还有那个悄悄吊打付费版的免费工具。真实账号、真实退订、零 affiliate 链接——我说这些没人给我一分钱。

script.img_zh: 过肩镜头，创作者指向屏幕里 5 个 App 图标，部分标『退订』部分标『保留』，霓虹青色点缀，超精细 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0

script.en: Here's the trap I was in, and maybe you are too. Every single week a new AI tool drops with a thumbnail screaming 'make ten thousand dollars with AI' or 'this one tool replaced my whole job.' So I'd sign up, pay the free trial, forget to cancel, and a month later there's another twenty bucks gone that I genuinely cannot explain. By January I was paying for seven different AI subscriptions at once, and not one of them had made me a single actual dollar. I wasn't running a business. I was collecting receipts for somebody else's startup. That's the exact moment I stopped trusting the marketing and decided to test, for real, what these tools actually do when you actually use them.
script.zh: 先说我掉进的坑，可能你也在里面。每周都有新 AI 工具冒出来，缩略图写着『用 AI 月入一万刀』『这一个工具替你干了全公司的活』。于是我注册、付试用、忘记取消，一个月后又是 20 刀莫名其妙没了。到一月份我同时在付 7 个 AI 订阅，没一个真给我赚到一毛钱。我不是在搞事业，我是在给别人的创业公司攒收据。就是那一刻我决定不再信营销，真的去测这些工具到底能干嘛。
script.viz: 手机里一排 AI 订阅扣款通知，创作者扶额
script.img_en: Phone screen full of AI subscription charge notifications, creator hand on forehead, dim warm 2am room, ultra-detailed 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0
script.img_zh: 手机屏幕满是 AI 订阅扣款通知，创作者手扶额，凌晨昏暗暖光房，超精细 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0

script.en: Here are the five tools, in the order I bought them. Tool one, a twenty-nine-dollar-a-month AI writing assistant that promises to write your client emails and land you freelance gigs. Tool two, a thirty-nine-dollar AI video generator that claims to make faceless YouTube videos while you sleep. Tool three, a nineteen-dollar AI resume and cover-letter builder for job hunts. Tool four, a forty-nine-dollar 'AI business in a box' that says it'll build you a whole online store with one prompt. And tool five, a completely free AI spreadsheet analyzer I threw in as my control group. My test method was deliberately simple and fair: for thirty full days I used each tool for its exact advertised job, tracked every hour it saved me and every dollar it earned me, and wrote down what really happened. No tricks, no scripting the outcome. Just honest daily use. Let me walk you through what each one actually did, starting with the most disappointing.
script.zh: 这 5 个工具，按我买的顺序。第一个，29 刀/月的 AI 写作助手，号称帮你写客户邮件、接自由职业活。第二个，39 刀的 AI 视频生成器，号称你睡着它替你做无人出镜 YouTube。第三个，19 刀的 AI 简历/求职信生成器。第四个，49 刀的『AI 一键开店盒子』，说一个 prompt 就给你搭好网店。第五个，一个完全免费的 AI 表格分析器，我拿来当对照组。我的测试方法故意简单公平：整整 30 天，每个工具只干它广告里说的那个活，记录省下的每一小时和赚到的每一块钱，把真实发生的事写下来。不耍花招，不篡改结果，就是老实用。下面从最让人失望的那个讲起。
script.viz: 屏幕列出 5 个工具卡片带价格，鼠标依次点亮
script.img_en: Screen showing 5 tool cards in a row with prices, mouse cursor tracing through them, dark IDE background neon teal, ultra-detailed 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0
script.img_zh: 屏幕里横排 5 张工具卡片带价格，鼠标依次划过，深色 IDE 背景霓虹青，超精细 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0

script.en: Tool one, the writing assistant — total waste. It produced emails that sounded like a robot pretending to be confident, and two of my clients literally asked if I'd been replaced by software. Zero freelance gigs landed. Tool three, the resume builder — also a waste. It spat out a generic template I ended up rewriting from scratch anyway, so it saved me nothing and just cost me nineteen dollars. And tool four, the forty-nine-dollar business-in-a-box, was the biggest letdown of all. It generated a storefront stuffed with placeholder products and a checkout button that didn't even work, and when I messaged support they sent me a link to a YouTube tutorial. I paid forty-nine dollars a month to be told to watch a video. So there it is: three tools, a hundred and seven dollars a month combined, and not one single dollar earned back. That's the part that should make you a little angry.
script.zh: 第一个，写作助手——纯浪费。它写的邮件像机器人假装自信，两个客户直接问我是不是被软件取代了。零单自由职业。第三个，简历生成器——也浪费。吐出来一个通用模板，我最后还是从头重写，啥也没省，白交 19 刀。最坑的是第四个，49 刀的开店盒子。它生成的店铺塞满占位商品，结账按钮根本点不动，我找客服，对方丢给我一个 YouTube 教程链接。我一个月交 49 刀，就为了被人叫去看视频。所以结论：3 个工具，一个月合计 107 刀，一分钱没赚回来。这地方该让你有点火大。
script.viz: 分屏：3 张红 X 收据 vs 退订页面，翻白眼
script.img_en: Split screen three red-X receipts labeled $29/$19/$49 vs a cancellation page, creator rolling eyes, dark UI, ultra-detailed 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0
script.img_zh: 分屏：三张红 X 收据标 29/19/49 刀 vs 退订页面，创作者翻白眼，深色 UI，超精细 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0

script.en: Now the two that actually paid for themselves. Tool two, the thirty-nine-dollar video generator — this one genuinely earned its keep. I used it to produce five short faceless videos for a tiny affiliate page I'd abandoned, and two of them started trickling in around forty dollars in commission over the month. Not life-changing money, but it more than covered its own subscription. But the real shock was tool five, the free spreadsheet analyzer. I fed it my affiliate earnings and my ad spend, and within seconds it flagged a tracking mistake that had been quietly draining about sixty dollars a month from me for almost a year. The free tool caught a leak that the paid forty-nine-dollar 'business in a box' never even mentioned. So here's the final scoreboard: two tools paid off, the free one beat a paid one, and I'm hitting cancel on the other three right after this video.
script.zh: 现在说那两个真回本的。第二个，39 刀的视频生成器——这个真值回票价。我用它给我一个荒废的小联盟页做了 5 条无人出镜短视频，其中 2 条一个月陆续带来约 40 刀佣金。不算改变人生，但够 cover 它自己的订阅还有余。真正的震惊是第五个，免费的表格分析器。我把联盟收入和广告支出喂进去，它几秒就揪出一个追踪错误——这个错误悄悄每个月吞掉我约 60 刀，快一年了。免费工具发现的漏洞，那个 49 刀『开店盒子』提都没提。最终战绩：2 个回本、免费的干翻付费的、剩下 3 个我今天就退订。
script.viz: 左手举『+40 佣金』便签，右手举『免费工具赢』卡片
script.img_en: Creator holding '+$40 commission' sticky in left hand and 'FREE tool wins' card in right, confident smile, dark studio RGB, ultra-detailed 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0
script.img_zh: 创作者左手举『+40 刀佣金』便签、右手举『免费工具赢』卡片，自信微笑，深色 RGB 工作室，超精细 8k --ar 16:9 --v 6.0

script.en: So what's the actual rule for not lighting money on fire with AI tools? Here's what thirty days taught me. First, if a tool promises to make you money without you doing any of the work, it is lying to your face — every single tool that paid off simply saved me time on work I was already doing, not one of them magically printed cash. Second, always keep one free tool as your control group, because the paid ones are literally counting on you never running the comparison. And third, the part that really stings: the most expensive tool was the worst value, not the best. So before you subscribe to anything, ask yourself one brutal question — 'What specific task am I already doing that this thing will actually save me time on?' If you cannot name that task in five seconds, that is your answer, and it's don't buy. The AI gold rush is absolutely real, but most of the gold is being sold, not found.
script.zh: 那到底怎么才能不在 AI 工具上烧钱？30 天教会我三件事。第一，凡是号称『不用你干活就能搞钱』的工具，都是在当面骗你——每个回本的工具，都只是帮我省下了我本来就在做的工作的时间，没一个凭空印钞。第二，永远留一个免费工具当对照组，因为付费工具赌的就是你从不比较。第三，最扎心的一点：最贵的那个价值最低，不是最高。所以订阅任何东西前，问自己一个狠问题——『我已经在做的、这个能帮我省时间的，具体是哪件事？』如果 5 秒答不上来，答案就是别买。AI 淘金热是真的，但大部分金子是被卖出来的，不是被挖出来的。

script.en: Here's the one line I want you to remember: the best AI tool for making money is the one that saves you time on work you're already good at — never the one with the loudest thumbnail. The full ledger, with every tool, its real price, and exactly what it earned or lost, is linked in the description, free, no email gate. If this video just saved you two hundred bucks, smash that subscribe button. Next week I'm testing the completely free alternatives to all five tools, so you literally never have to pay again. I'll see you there.
script.zh: 记住这一句：最能帮你搞钱的 AI 工具，是帮你省下『你本来就很擅长的工作』时间的那个——绝不是缩略图喊得最响的那个。完整账本，每个工具、真实价格、赚或亏多少，都在简介链接里，免费、不要邮箱。如果这条视频帮你省了 200 刀，按一下订阅。下周我测这 5 个工具的完全免费平替，让你再也不用花钱。那里见。

titles: Investing vs Paying Off Debt: The Order That Saves You $31,000
Why Paying Off Your 22% Credit Card Is the Best Investment You'll Ever Make

script.en: Every finance influencer says 'invest first, always'. They're half right. If you have a 22% credit card, paying it off is a guaranteed 22% return. No stock on earth beats that.
script.zh: 每个理财博主都在说『先投资，永远先投资』。他们对了一半。如果你有一张 22% 的信用卡，先还清它就是锁定一笔无风险的 22% 回报。地球上没有任何股票能稳定跑赢这个。

script.en: Here's the trap that costs Americans $31,000 over ten years. Investing feels like winning. Every time you check your brokerage, the number goes up. You feel smart. Paying off debt feels like admitting you messed up. Every payment reminds you of the dinner you didn't need, the vacation you charged, the impulse you regret. So people choose the thing that feels good instead of the thing that makes them money. And it's not a small mistake. On $8,000 of credit card debt at 22% APR, choosing to invest $500 a month instead of paying it off costs you roughly $31,000 over ten years. That's a car. That's a down payment on a house. That's your kid's first year of college. All burned on a feeling. The market does 7% after inflation. Your card does 22% against you. You're not 'diversifying'. You're paying a 22% subscription fee to feel smart. That's the trap.
script.zh: 有一个陷阱，让美国人在十年里烧掉 31,000 美元。投资让人感觉像在赢。每次你打开券商 App，数字往上跳，你就觉得自己很聪明。还债让人感觉像在承认自己搞砸了。每一次还款都提醒你那顿不该吃的饭、那趟不该刷的旅行、那次冲动的后悔。所以人选让自己感觉好的那件事，不选让自己真赚钱的那件事。这不是小错。8,000 美元信用卡债、22% 年利率，本来应该拿 500 美元去还债，你拿去投资，十年下来大概亏 31,000 美元。够买一辆车，够交房子首付，够你孩子第一年大学。全部烧在一种感觉上。扣除通胀后市场长期回报 7%，你的卡以 22% 反向吸你。你这不是『分散投资』，是付 22% 的订阅费买『我很聪明』的感觉。这就是那个坑。

script.en: Three lines. Line one — write down the highest APR you owe. Line two — write down 7%, the long-run average of the S&P 500 after inflation. Line three — if your APR is higher than 7%, the guaranteed return of paying it off beats the expected return of investing. That's the whole test. So if your credit card is 22%, paying it off is a 22% guaranteed return. If your federal student loan is 6%, that's basically break-even with the market — flip a coin. If your mortgage is 3.5%, you almost certainly invest first because the spread is in your favor. The math is simple. The hard part is the next thing — the psychology — which is where smart people lose money on purpose. Because here's what nobody tells you: the math isn't the hard part. Following the math when it tells you to do the unsexy thing is the hard part.
script.zh: 三行。第一行——写下你欠的最高年利率。第二行——写下 7%，即扣除通胀后 S&P 500 的长期平均回报。第三行——如果你的年利率高于 7%，还清它的『保证回报』就高于投资的『预期回报』。这就是整个测试。所以如果你的卡是 22%，还清它就是一笔锁定的 22% 回报。如果你的联邦学生贷款是 6%，和市场基本打平——掷硬币。如果你的房贷是 3.5%，几乎一定先投资，因为利差站在你这边。数学很简单，难的是下一关——心理——那才是聪明人故意亏钱的地方。因为没人告诉你这一点：数学本身不难。难的是当数学告诉你做那件『不性感』的事时，你愿不愿意做。

script.en: Three real numbers. Person A has $8,000 on a 22% card and $500 a month to split. They invest first because that's what they read online. After ten years they have $11,000 in investments and $42,000 of credit card debt — because the debt grew faster than the investments could keep up. Person B — same $8,000, same $500 a month. They ignore the advice, pay off the card in 19 months, then invest the full $500. After ten years they have $89,000. No debt. Person C: $3,000 on a 5% card, $500 a month. They split 50/50 for 7 months, kill the card, then invest the full $500. Net at ten years: $76,000 and zero debt. The decision isn't moral. It isn't about discipline. It's arithmetic. And the arithmetic says: kill the 22% first. Always. Same starting dollars, same monthly amount, three completely different lives ten years later. The only difference was the order. You can argue about investing strategies your whole life. You cannot argue about this order.
script.zh: 三个真实数字。A 君有 8,000 美元 22% 的卡，每月能拿出 500 美元。他先投资，因为网上都这么教。十年后他有 11,000 美元的投资，和 42,000 美元的信用卡债——因为债长得比投资快。B 君——同样的 8,000，同样的 500。他他不建议，先把卡 19 个月还清，再把 500 美元全投进去。十年后他有 89,000 美元。无债一身轻。C 君：3,000 美元 5% 的卡，每月 500。先 50/50 分 7 个月，把卡砍掉，再把 500 美元全投。十年净：76,000 美元，零债务。这不是道德题，不是纪律题，是算术题。算术说：先杀 22%，永远。一样的本金，一样的月供，三条十年后完全不同的路。唯一区别是顺序。你可以为投资策略争论一辈子，这一笔顺序不能争。

script.en: Three traps keep smart people stuck. Trap one — 'I have a 0% APR promo for 12 months.' That's not a real rate, that's a marketing rate. When the promo ends, it jumps to 25%. Don't make a 10-year decision on a 12-month promo. Trap two — 'I'll invest and use the gains to pay off the card.' The math doesn't work. 22% debt versus 7% expected market return is a 15-point spread. You will lose. Every time. The 'gains' don't outrun the interest. Trap three — 'I need an emergency fund first.' Yes, you do — keep one month of expenses in cash, no more. But if your emergency fund earns 4.5% in a high-yield savings and your card is at 22%, your emergency fund is costing you 17.5% a year. Move the excess to the card. The point isn't that emergencies don't happen. The point is the math doesn't lie. And the moment you add emotion — 'I want to feel like I'm investing', 'I don't want to face how much I owe' — the math stops mattering to you, and the banks start winning.
script.zh: 三个坑让聪明人原地踏步。坑一——『我有 12 个月 0% APR 的促销。』那不是真利率，是营销利率。促销一结束，它跳到 25%。别拿 12 个月的促销去做 10 年的决定。坑二——『我投资赚的够我去还信用卡。』数学说不通。22% 的债对 7% 的市场预期，15 个点的利差，你会输。每次都输。赚的『收益』跑不过利息。坑三——『我得先存够应急金。』对，要存——留一个月开支在现金里，但别更多。如果你的应急金在 HYSA 里拿 4.5%，而你的卡是 22%，你的应急金一年倒亏你 17.5%。把多余的部分挪去还卡。重点不是『应急不会发生』，重点是『数学不骗人』。一旦你开始加情绪——『我想感觉自己也在投资』『我不想面对我欠了多少』——数学在你眼里就失效了，银行就开始赢。

script.en: One exception overrides everything else. If your employer offers a 401k match, take the match first, always, no matter what. A 50% employer match on 6% of your salary is a 50% instant return on your contribution. Nothing else in your financial life will give you that. Not real estate. Not index funds. Not crypto. Not a side hustle. Free money first, always. So the order becomes: match → high-interest debt → low-interest debt → invest the rest. And if your employer offers ESPP at a 15% discount, same logic — take the discount, then deal with the debt. The one time you don't follow the math is when someone is handing you free money. That's the exception. Walk past it and you leave 50% returns on the table for the entire rest of your career. Compounded over 30 years, a missed match can cost you $300,000 or more. That's not a budgeting tip. That's a quarter-million-dollar decision you're making every pay period you skip.
script.zh: 一个例外能推翻其他一切。如果你的公司给 401k 配比，先拿满配比，永远先拿，无论别的什么。公司按你工资 6% 给 50% 的配比，等于你那一笔 50% 的即时回报。你整个财务生活里，再也没有别的东西能给你这个回报。房地产不行，加密币不行，副业不行。先拿免费的钱，永远。所以顺序变成：先配比 → 再清高息债 → 再清低息债 → 最后才投剩下的。如果公司给 ESPP 15% 折扣，同样的逻辑——先拿折扣，再处理债务。唯一可以不看数学的时刻，是有人正在把免费的钱递到你手上的时候。这就是那个例外。你走过去，等于把接下来整个职业生涯的 50% 回报让出去。复利 30 年，错过的配比可以让你亏掉 30 万美元以上。这不是预算技巧，是你每个发薪日都在做的、几十万级别的决定。

script.en: Here's the line I want you to remember. The best investor in the world is the one who refuses to pay 22% interest to a credit card company. That's not a budget tip. That's the highest-returning investment you'll ever make. Run the 3-question test tonight. Pay off the 22% before you put another dollar in an index fund. The 4-line decision tree and the 3-trap checklist are linked in the description — free, no email gate. If this saved you $31,000, hit subscribe. Next week I'm doing the order for paying off multiple cards when you can only afford to attack one at a time. See you there.
script.zh: 这是我希望你记住的那句话。世界上最厉害的投资人，就是那个拒绝给信用卡公司交 22% 利息的人。这不是预算技巧，这是你这辈子回报最高的投资。今晚就跑一遍那个 3 问测试。在你再投一块钱进指数基金之前，先把那张 22% 的卡砍掉。4 行决策树 + 3 个陷阱清单，简介里免费，不要邮箱。如果这条视频给你省了 31,000 美元，按一下订阅。下周我做『同时欠多张卡、每月只够砍一张』的顺序。看那里见。

packages.description: 你有 8,000 美元 22% 的信用卡债，先投资还是先还债？本视频用真实利率算清：还清高息债等于无风险锁 22%，几乎没有投资能稳定跑赢。展示三个真实美国人的 10 年对比（A 君 $11k 投资 + $42k 债 vs B 君 $89k 无债 vs C 君 $76k 无债），给出正确顺序——401k 配比 → 高息债 → 低息债 → 再投资；并解释三个让聪明人也亏钱的坑（0% 促销 / 投资覆盖利息 / 应急金过多）。教育/演示内容，不构成个别投资建议；利率与历史回报请回 Federal Reserve / NY Fed / S&P 一手来源核实（发布前自行核对）。订阅看更多美国人该懂的理财硬知识，下周讲『同时欠多张卡、每月只够砍一张』的顺序。
